newsitem.title: GERMANY: BASF shares gain strongly in early trade.
newsitem.headline: BASF shares gain strongly in early trade.

text.p: Shares in German chemical giant BASF AG advanced strongly in early trade after the group said it expected to post stronger 1997 earnings and an increase in sales.
BASF shares pushed to 62 marks in early electronic trade, before settling back to 61.45 marks in pre-bourse trade, a rise of 80 pfennigs or around 1.3 percent.

BASF's gain came against a background of a higher overall market, recovering from Tuesday's correction. The IBIS DAX index was up 22.70 points, or 0.69 percent, at 3,304.16 points in pre-bourse trade.
Dealers said the market was enthusiastic about the group's 1996 earnings per share (EPS), while the rest of the figures announced earlier were generally in line with expectations.
"The outlook was good. It was cautious, but then we've come to expect that from BASF," a Frankfurt trader.
Positive sentiment on the chemical sector helped lift other stocks. Bayer AG was up 1.42 percent at 68.60 marks, while Hoechst was up 68 pfennigs, over one percent, at 65.08 marks.
